title: Historical time preserves source precision, observation and knowledge boundaries
failure_signature: A coarse or unknown historical time is silently sharpened into an exact date, a computational range boundary is presented as the occurrence date, unknown onset is confused with an as-of observation, or later-known information becomes visible before its conservative knowledge boundary.
root_cause: Temporal semantics arrived incrementally under real Kemerton/Kwinana replay pressure. Treating every stored timestamp as the same kind of time can erase source precision, collapse period/timeless/unknown, backdate an observed state to a fabricated onset, or manufacture day-level Outcome error.
invariant: Historical records preserve the source-supported time expression: valid/target/outcome ranges plus precision/text, explicit period/timeless/unknown kind, optional observation/as-of time when onset is unknown, and a separate conservative known-time. Range endpoints may be computational bounds but are never evidence that an event occurred on the boundary day. Outcome timing is compared only at precision supported by both target and outcome.
anti_regression: Do not coerce month/quarter/year/range/approximate evidence into a fake exact day or instant for sorting, UI or scoring.
Do not infer timeless versus unknown from null valid-time bounds.
Do not set valid_from to an observation/as-of date merely because the state was observed then; unknown onset remains unknown.
Do not relax conservative known-time/no-lookahead because occurrence time is coarse or uncertain.
Do not report day-level Outcome delay/error when the Judgment target or realized outcome only supports coarser precision.

guards.description: Judgment targets preserve source-supported temporal precision.

guards.contains: must not manufacture day-level timing error
guards.description: Outcome timing cannot invent finer error precision than target/outcome support.

guards.contains: state is true as of T; onset unknown
guards.description: Canonical Reality keeps observation/as-of separate from unknown onset.
A month represented with computational bounds is not claimed to occur on its first day.

revisit_when: Only revisit if a replacement temporal model can still round-trip source wording/precision, distinguish period/timeless/unknown, represent observed-as-of with unknown onset, preserve conservative known-time and compare Outcome timing without false precision.
